title: Tax Subsidy Information and Local Economic Effects

scopes.description: Complete author-documented workflow: R county employment panel construction, Stata subsidy preparation and county regressions, subsequent-subsidy descriptives, MSU state-year preparation, and the separate state/program-year disclosure analyses. The active main-analysis path excludes megadeals; its documented inclusion alternative is retained separately with its own unresolved sample input. The order between the MSU merge producer, county panel, subsidy sample and later state/program models also remains unresolved.

requirements.description: The R county-construction entry point reads the annual QCEW NAICS single-file series for 2001–2019, filters to selected industries, ownerships and aggregation levels, then constructs state/county/national outputs. issues.description: The archive includes programs and documentation but no empirical input datasets. The active workflow references public products, author-prepared tables and manual classifications; most exact versions, fields or histories remain unverified and are listed as separate requirements.

These are supported setup/staging handoffs between the supplied programs: R writes Data/countydata_agg_updated2022.csv and Stata imports the same county-panel basename from its current directory; the MSU cleaner writes cleaned_msu_data_final and the state/program script reads that same state-year product under StateGovt/; the main driver calls ../Code/Estimations paths while the registered supplied programs are flat. A local project root and directory/staging layout can resolve these known same-product paths while preserving the supplied records and code. No specific data or schema mismatch is established by the path differences; original author directory identity is not required.

create_subsidy_data_final.do merges county_years_in_sample_final before regressions_final.do creates that file later. The driver explicitly instructs a later subsidy-data rerun. The supplied materials do not specify the first-run seed or the exact post-run rerun sequence, so the producer/consumer cycle needs author clarification and a staged procedure.

The main subsidy workflow and the separate state/program analysis consume program_level_disclosure_years, but its only supplied workbook-import producer is commented out and references an unlisted workbook. The author-described 27-jurisdiction statute review and required fields are known; the exact active input, version and construction handoff are not.

The only shown county education and population construction blocks are commented out, but later active code merges educ_county_year and county_pop_25_64. The documented 2008 education workbook and Census population source do not close the exact historical series or intermediate production contract.

The supplied main analysis defaults to excluding megadeal counties and explicitly documents a comment-out alternative to include them. The subsidy program also builds a separate megadeal-inclusive sample output from county_years_in_sample_with_megadeals_2023_03_31, whose producer is not supplied. The alternative is therefore preserved as a distinct unresolved branch rather than silently treated as the baseline or as a verified option.

County preprocessing consumes StateGovt/cleaned_msu_data_final_for_merging, which the separate state/program script produces. Later in that same state/program script, analyses consume subsidies_in_final_sample from subsidy preparation and control_variables_all from county preprocessing. The main driver runs subsidy preparation and county preprocessing before the later county sample is created, and it does not call the separate state/program script. The archive does not specify the staged/bootstrap passes needed to satisfy all of these producer/consumer dependencies without skipping a branch.

review_notes: Scope includes R county construction, MSU state-year preparation, the main county regressions, subsequent-subsidy descriptives, and the independent state/program-year analyses.
Generated outputs are classified from active source producers; they do not require pre-existing populated probes. Raw inputs and unresolved producer/consumer order are assessed separately.
The screening incident is recorded in probes/screening_incident.json and is not cited as workflow evidence; candidate content and adjacent screened lines are excluded from this assessment.
Public-page fetch failures are preserved in probes/public_inspection_failures_v001.json as inspection limits only; they do not establish restricted access or unavailable data.
Requirements keep independent source products, author spreadsheets and manual classifications separate; common schemas are not treated as equivalent datasets.
The R source actively reads several auxiliary CSVs that are not used downstream in the supplied file. They remain runtime requirements pending author confirmation of removable reads.

The public BLS QCEW route is verified for the annual 2001–2019 product. BEA, Census, Berkeley and IPPSR pages identify candidate source families, while exact author contracts remain unverified where stated.
All 31 frozen dependency IDs are reviewed individually. Active data reads map to distinct logical requirements; source-produced intermediates and unresolved producers are distinguished.

The flat package inventory contains the four active main-driver helper files, while the driver names a separate ../Code/Estimations layout; this remains a project-root/staging issue rather than an absent-program claim.
Every nonlocal or unverified input, unavailable software item, and unresolved issue has a linked action; no source edits, downloads, installs or author execution were performed.
The verified public product route is BLS QCEW. BEA GDP and other official/repository candidate sources remain unverified where exact table units, vintage or author fields are unresolved.
The official QCEW annual layout exposes annual_avg_estabs_count; the R script expects annual_avg_estabs, so the supported input route includes a one-column rename in the prepared CSV.
Frozen catalog lookups used the registered helper copy and remained discovery-only; unrelated metadata matches and zero exact candidates were not treated as access or availability findings.
The main driver's active baseline excludes megadeal counties; the explicitly documented inclusion alternative and its separate sample input/output remain a distinct unresolved branch.

Additional generated handoffs are source-proven: the clean-name mapping and subsidy-by-type dataset are produced by subsidy preparation, and the StateGovt MSU merge dataset is produced by the separate state/program script before county preprocessing. These outputs do not require pre-existing populated probes.

A separate cross-branch order issue records that county preprocessing consumes an MSU merge output from the state/program script, while later state/program models consume subsidy and control intermediates from the main branch. No unsupported staged order is assumed.

The exact local project root is a setup choice: source-supported same-product relative paths can be resolved by directory staging/configuration. This does not resolve the separate county sample cycle, cross-branch ordering, or unknown input contracts.
